Q: Convert raw MySQL query with SUM() expressions containing multiple conditions to CodeIgniter's query builder A:

What is consistently enforced in all of your SUM() expressions is:

  • invite.friendID = $mID and
  • evnt.ends >= '$event_ts' and
  • invite.isactive = 0 and
  • evnt.isactive = 0

This means that those filters should be moved from the expressions in the SELECT clause to the WHERE clause.

If you don't want to make repeated select_sum() calls, you can use the D.R.Y. practice of declaring an array of the variable parts and implementing a loop.

public function getInvitationSummary(int $mID, string $event_ts): array
{
    $conditions = [
        'undecided' => [
            "invite.decidedwhen = '0000-00-00 00:00:00'",
        ],
        'yes' => [
            "invite.decidedwhen != '0000-00-00 00:00:00'",
            'invite.yes = 1',
        ],
        'no' => [
            "invite.decidedwhen != '0000-00-00 00:00:00'",
            'invite.no = 1',
        ],
        'maybe' => [
            "invite.decidedwhen != '0000-00-00 00:00:00'",
            'invite.maybe = 1',
        ]   
    ];
    array_walk(
        $conditions,
        fn($rules, $alias) => $this->db->select_sum(implode(' AND ', $rules), $alias);
    );
    return (array)$this->db
        ->join('user_event evnt', 'eID')
        ->get_where('user_event_invite invite', [
            'invite.friendID' => $mID,
            'evnt.ends >=' => $event_ts,
            'invite.isactive' => 0,
            'evnt.isactive' => 0,
        ])
        ->row_array();
}

The result set of the above query will always return a single row, but because CodeIgniter's row_array() method signature indicates that null is a possible return type, I'll explicitly cast the result as an array to inform IDEs.

The returned array will have the same keys as the $conditions array.

Q: Comparing two Dates in Java A:

compareTo

You misunderstand the purpose of compareTo. Read the Javadoc.

The compareTo method returns “a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as this object is less than, equal to, or greater than the specified object”. The compareTo method does not tell you anything about elapsed time.

Tip: Programming by documentation > Programming by intuition.

Avoid legacy date-time classes

Never use the terribly-flawed legacy classes such as Date, Calendar, SimpleDateFormat, etc.

Use only the modern java.time classes built into Java 8 and later.

java.time.LocalDate

To represent a date-only value, use LocalDate class.

Define a formatting pattern to match your non-standard input.

DateTimeFormatter formatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern( "MM-dd-uuuu" );

Parse.

LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse( "06/18/2015" , formatter ) ;

java.time.Period

Calculate elapsed time on a scale of years-months-days as a Period.

Period period = Period.between( someDate , otherDate ) ;

ChronoUnit.DAYS

Or get the number of days between dates.

long days = ChronoUnit.DAYS.between( someDate , otherDate ) ;

Q: 'Field required a bean of type that could not be found.' error Spring RESTful API using MongoDB A:

Add the annotation @ComponentScan, along with @Configuration to your MainApplication and then you’re are good to go.

@ComponentScan without arguments tells Spring to scan the current package and all of its subpackages.

Q: How to sync a Python List of Canvas IDs with canvas.delete("all") to avoid errors in an Undo function? A:

I think the cleanest is to just clear history with every delete all call.

Create your own clear_canvas_and_history function that includes both steps. A strong benefit of this approach is that should be easy to modify later if you decide a different approach makes more sense.

Below is a example code to do this.

## Add new function by undo
def clear_canvas_and_history():
    canvas.delete("all") # handles current setup
    history.clear() # resets history list (in-place, global list)

## Be sure to update what is being called!
btn_clear = Button(root, text="Clear All",
                   command=clear_canvas_and_history)
